scope: Sources reviewed to test whether Uganda June 2 and June 5 2022 police fatalities, UCDP GED25.1 444765 and 444764, meet state-based battle-related conflict definitions. HTML read publicly during this research; pages not archived by SHA. Media republication does not produce independent eyewitnesses.

sources.supports: Reports separate June 2 Old Kampala foiled robbery killing and June 5 Makindye operation killing; police alleges money-laundering/robbery for ADF, not independently verified individual dyad status
sources.limitations: Involved police service; distinguishes alleged affiliation of arrested people from details of the two deceased

sources.supports: Repeats police spokesperson's statements about shootings and funding allegations
sources.limitations: No separate crime scene witness, shooter, medical record or rebel organization declaration

sources.supports: Distinguishes police descriptions of Makindye and Old Kampala; repeats police account
sources.limitations: Not independent verification of IS membership or a politically motivated armed exchange

sources.supports: Names separate killed persons but attributes material facts to Police spokesperson Fred Enanga
sources.limitations: Media institution distinct from police but underlying event testimony is the same police briefing

sources.supports: Reports another senior security officer stating that operatives located a June 5 deceased robbery suspect at Kyeyagalire and killed him at the house
sources.limitations: Different interviewee but still state security institution; statement may be compatible with police resisting-arrest narrative and cannot resolve force justification; does not independently prove ADF combatant status

sources.supports: Reproduces the anonymous senior officer's narrative of the June 5 killing
sources.limitations: Editorial reuse of the same security-officer interview, not a new eyewitness

sources.supports: Defines state-based armed conflict by stated government/territory incompatibility and armed force between warring parties; separately defines battle-related deaths and per-dyad >=25 activity
sources.limitations: Methodological rule, not evidence about two individual deaths

sources.supports: Event-level fatal organized violence and source independence; official notes historic dyad inclusion after threshold crossing
sources.limitations: Methodological rule, not an independent victim witness

dependencies.basis: Attributes shooting, terrorism funding and suspects to same police spokesperson
Attributes observations and key assertions to police spokesperson
Attributes original facts of 2 and 5 June to police spokesperson
Shares senior-security-officer interview published by/attributed to URN; publication-to-publication editorial dependency not independently proven, but both use same officer claim

event_claims.official_death_report: Police reports killing during violent counter operation and alleged resistance
event_claims.other_official_testimony: Later security commander says operatives located him at home and killed him; no independent confirmation of who fired first or any rebel engagement
event_claims.reason: Police killing during arrest/anti-robbery operation plus alleged terror-financing link not sufficient alone to establish exchange of armed force between parties to territorial/governmental conflict

event_claims.official_death_report: Police reports killing during foiled commercial robbery
event_claims.reason: Reported robbery by person police associates with fundraising gang; no independently identified armed conflict encounter or direct affiliation of this deceased person to IS under UCDP rules

independence_conclusion: Four June articles have one identified original event reporter: police spokesperson. September two publications use another police-security interviewee, but still no nonstate eyewitness, victim family account or independent conflict status confirmation in sources reviewed. Do not mistake 6 publications for 6 independent witnesses.
conflict_eligibility_conclusion: Two reported killings and separate identities are supported by official source, but whether they qualify as Government of Uganda vs IS state-based battle deaths is unresolved in publicly examined material. No evidence demonstrates a source coding error. Ask UCDP coders for dyad-specific basis before proposing reclassification.
